tone_statements.quote: Burushaski has a pitch accent system. An accented vowel is pronounced with a high pitch. I indicate such high-pitched vowels with the diacritic ˊ. This accent is distinctive: e.g., íne ‘he (DIST) :ERG/GEN’ vs. iné ‘that (H): ABS’; one word has one accent in principle (but some words have two accents synchronically). The pitch of accented long vowels must be high or a gradual fall (indicated as áa). If vowels take the pitch pattern of a rising tone (indicated as aá), they should be considered as not long vowels but vowel sequences with two identical vowels in two syllables, for example, /a.á/.
tone_statements.summary: Distinctive pitch accent: accented vowel = high pitch, one accent per word in principle (íne vs iné); noun accent stays in the stem, verbal prefixes can attract it; no tone count; stress not treated.

sources.quote: Burushaski has five short vowels: i, e, a, o, u, and five long bi-moraic ones: ii, ee, aa, oo, uu. The stress may fall on either of the two morae.
sources.note: INCIDENTAL, NOT THE WANTED WORK: this sentence is from the next section, 1.10.2 'The Burushaski language' by Etienne Tiffou, which the proof PDF includes because it starts on the same page (165) where Abbi's section ends. Impressionistic (no measurement), first-hand author sketch; says stress can sit on either mora of a long vowel, i.e. long vowels carry a contrastive stress position; no statement on stress placement in short-vowel words, secondary stress or domain (section truncated at p. 165).glott

sources.quote: For the Srinagar (J&K) diaspora variety only: 'the distribution of stress in JKB appears to be sensitive to quantitative (syllable weight), positional ... and (perhaps) rhythmic ... constraints. Every content word in JKB is stressed. Stress is iambic and iterative.' Generalizations: (a) heavy syllables (closed or long-vowel) always stressed; (b) rightmost heavy gets primary stress; (c) final CV never stressed; (d) in CV sequences the second syllable is stressed if non-final, disyllabic CV.CV initial; (e) in inflected verbs stress is determined by the verb stem, pronominal prefixes inside the d
